title: Fourier restriction estimates based on $L^q$-dimensions: beyond Stein--Tomas
summary: The well-known Stein--Tomas restriction theorem gives the sharp range of $p$ for which $L^p\to L^2$ restriction estimates hold for the surface measure on the sphere. This was generalised to arbitrary measures satisfying certain Fourier decay and Frostman conditions by Mockenhaupt, Mitsis, and Bak--Seeger, with the most general version now a fundamental result in harmonic analysis. The Frostman condition essentially asks for uniform control on the measure of small balls and is the endpoint of a continuum of more nuanced conditions which describe the local fluctuations of the measure.
